overview.summary: Sanofi's strategy centers on Dupixent dominance across Type 2 inflammation (AD, asthma, CRSwNP, COPD, EoE, prurigo nodularis) while building a next-gen immunology pipeline (amlitelimab, itepekimab). The company is executing a portfolio transformation—divesting its Consumer Healthcare unit (Opella) and doubling down on specialty immunology and rare disease. Dupixent alone accounts for ~30% of pharma revenue and is Almirall's single largest competitive threat in atopic dermatitis.
keyStrengths: Dupixent franchise: $16B+ blockbuster expanding into 10+ indications
Amlitelimab (anti-OX40L): next-gen biologic positioned as Dupixent successor
Market-leading KOL network in dermatology and allergology
Deep real-world evidence base across all Dupixent indications
overview.threatRationale: Sanofi is Almirall's most direct and dangerous competitor. Dupixent dominates the moderate-to-severe AD biologic market where Ebglyss (lebrikizumab) competes. Sanofi's sales force, payer relationships, and indication breadth create switching inertia that Ebglyss must overcome. Additionally, amlitelimab (anti-OX40L) targets the same AD population with a potentially differentiated profile.
